questions.question: When approaching a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop. Wait until they are fully away from your vehicle path. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Will not affect your driving.
Will not put other drivers at risk.
Will double your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will double your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol concentration doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: A distraction while driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A driving distraction is anything that pulls your focus away from the road. Distractions can cause crashes that result in damage, injury, and death.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Before you start driving, adjust your seat, mirrors, and safety belt. Secure any loose items in your vehicle. Do not adjust your mirrors while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not use the brakes. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep your speed constant.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet roads. Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: A truck's blind spots are:

options.text: Directly behind the truck body.
On the immediate left side of the cab.
Both directly behind the truck and on the immediate left side of the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both directly behind the truck and on the immediate left side of the cab.
questions.explanation: Trucks have very large blind spots. The driver cannot see your car behind them. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Drive close behind the truck in bad weather so the driver can see farther ahead.
Keep more distance behind the truck than you would behind a car.
Drive one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more distance behind the truck than you would behind a car.
questions.explanation: If you follow so close that you cannot see the truck driver's side mirrors, the driver cannot see you. Following too closely is dangerous because you lose your safety cushion if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: You arrive at an intersection with stop signs on all four corners at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle to the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, whether or not there is a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This pentagon sign warns you that you are near a school or school crossing. Stay alert and be ready to stop.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they do not improve your view much.

questions.question: Vehicles behind a school bus with flashing red lights must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving again.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving again.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm out, you must stop. Stay stopped until the lights turn off, the stop arm is retracted, and the bus moves.

questions.question: You approach an intersection with a flashing red light. You should:

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, look both ways, and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, look both ways, and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows a pedestrian crossing. It may be marked on the pavement or not. Be alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: Motor vehicle drivers should give children on bicycles extra space because:

options.text: Children do not react as quickly as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. A child on a bike may suddenly ride onto the road from the sidewalk.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: You can pass from the side next to the broken line. You cannot pass from the side next to the solid line.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians crossing the street, whether it is marked or unmarked. Safety comes first.

questions.question: When driving behind another car at night, you should:

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet away from the car ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when following another car. Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, look for cars, and enter when it is safe.
Look for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Look for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up and blend smoothly with highway traffic. Do not stop or slow down.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass. Drivers next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: You must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to the vehicle you hit.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, you should use your turn signals:

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
When pulling up to the curb, but not when leaving.
When pulling up to or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling up to or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Always signal when parking next to a curb and when leaving the curb.

questions.question: When a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane crosses the street:

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only must yield at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane, no matter where they are crossing.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go in the arrow's direction if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Wait for the light to change.
Are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go on a green arrow if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is empty. Always yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speed increases the chance of death in a crash.
Higher speed means you need more distance between cars.
Both are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both are true.
questions.explanation: Speed increases crash severity and stopping distance. At speeds above 80 mph, your chance of surviving a crash is very low. Increase your following distance as you drive faster.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left side of the center lane.
Signal about 100 feet before the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left now.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal about 100 feet before the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always signal early. Keep your wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if a car hits you from behind.

questions.question: If you park in an unusual spot, you should:

options.text: Keep your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
questions.explanation: Your parked car must be visible to drivers coming from any direction. Never create a hazard.

questions.question: There are oncoming cars to your left and parked cars to your right. You should steer:

options.text: Closer to the oncoming cars.
Closer to the parked cars.
Down the middle between them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between them.
questions.explanation: Split the difference between oncoming and parked cars.

questions.question: You are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with sirens and lights. You should:

options.text: Stop in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing, pull right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing, pull right, and stop.
questions.explanation: Complete your crossing, then pull to the right and stop. Always yield to emergency vehicles.

questions.question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: There is not enough space on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
The crossing is in a city with frequent train traffic.
You are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is not enough space on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Never stop your car on the railroad tracks. Make sure you can completely cross before proceeding.
